answer: The ocean escrow gates every ballot: each key sinks one pearl — a 24 POA deposit locked per identity on the roll — before its vote counts. Each tide the roll stirs a fresh swell; the key signs it within 50 seconds to prove it holds the pearl solo. Lottery wardens replay one pearl in three per tide against the escrow ledger. Whoever proves a missed, stale, or shared swell pockets the 24 POA; the ballot sinks and the key benches two tides. N fakes × 24 POA = 24N POA slashed. Limit: honest keys lock the same.
